reviews.reason: Catalog table contract: the named role=table carries busy state and logical row/column counts; its CSS-grid header row owns six columnheaders, and each indexed virtual row owns five value cells and one action cell with a native Install button. AntD Listy 6.6.2 delegates to @rc-component/listy 1.2.3 and @rc-component/virtual-list 1.5.1; the latter’s viewport/filler and Listy item wrappers are divs. Swapping the table, either row, header, or either cell site independently would break native table ancestry; swapping all six would still leave the measured scrolling viewport, virtual wrappers and pagination sentinel in invalid native table positions. Separately, the footer status wraps an AntD Spin div while loading, which output cannot contain. Keep the logical table and the polite status without changing virtual scrolling, responsive layout, or installation.

URL q/cursor still seed independently editable search and reset pagination; DataTable.emptyText remains a ReactNode slot.

searchText is an editable Input.Search draft. onChange edits it independently; only onSearch trims/navigates the submitted q and clears cursor. The q effect synchronizes an externally changed URL value. The new infinite query has no old page-history state; deriving the input continuously from q would prevent unsubmitted typing. P21f reassessed 2026-11-17: Template catalog now owns an infinite cursor query, appended virtual-list rows, per-query in-flight loadMore guard and local file installation preview. Tests assert exact next cursor, retained loaded rows on continuation failure, query reset and upload permission/preview boundaries. Editable searchText still synchronizes external q while onSearch submits it. The old DataTable emptyText diagnostic is absent in wave3 and its review remains held; unsupported upload-status tag rationale is also untouched.

The source intentionally performs a per-item mutation/install sequence and records its individual receipt before advancing; request parallelization is a separate behavior/resource policy, not a missing await optimization. ExtensionUploadModal owns one upload batch transaction: queued/uploading/installing/challenge/error phases and per-file progress. Its loop processes server installation/risk overrides in selected order and patches the corresponding item before moving on; arbitrary parallelization could interleave confirmations and extension installs. Status is an asynchronous live announcement, not a form output calculation. Reassessed 2026-11-03: extension_center.install.upload gates batch start and confirmation. The ordered per-file upload/install/risk challenge loop and individual receipts remain intentionally sequential.
